brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.requirement: Holder for soldering iron while switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: Cell 1,0,0 topped with solid cover (cover:1,0,0;full;top) with two L-brackets (accessory:0#1,0#1 and accessory:0#1,0#4) forming raised cradle. Props show pliers on top representing iron resting off flammable surface. No dedicated iron prop exists; steel/heat-proof material not verified by configurator — plastic parts are 3D-printed so heat-resistance is unmet, shape only.

requirements.requirement: Two bins for solder and spare tips
requirements.evidence: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full holds solder-reel prop (prop:1); bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full holds tweezers prop (prop:2) as spare tips/small parts. Both full-depth hex bins provided.

finish.summary: Three-cell linear bench station: two bin cells for storage, one capped cell with dual L-brackets as elevated hot-iron holder. Dressed with solder reel and tweezers in bins and pliers on holder to demonstrate use. Capped and joint-locked, mesh clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
